study type: Secondary analysis of a multicenter prospective cohort study
exposure: Duration of neuraxial analgesia (<5 hours vs. >=5 hours)
cohort: Women with single- and full-term cephalic pregnancy in northern China
finding: Longer duration of neuraxial labor analgesia (over 5 hours) was associated with an increased risk of intrapartum maternal fever, which was related to adverse maternal outcomes but not significantly to neonatal outcomes within 6 weeks after delivery.
